edition: Discover — 13 November 2026 · Mirrors, Grails and Long Nights
intro: A room designed to evoke ghostly presences, a strange Winchester encounter, Gothic RPG worlds and a fresh dark-fantasy story. Sainthood, Faust and an Arthurian ballad bring the Christian and literary threads together. Nine recent picks plus an August 2025 Westeros gem. Retrospectives, mature themes and major spoilers are marked.

items.title: Scientists Used a 'Psychomanteum' to Summon Ghostly Encounters. Then It Got Weird.
items.summary: Thirty volunteers spent time in a dim room gazing toward a mirror, and 24 reported a sensed presence. Esra Öz examines the experiment, its unexpected camera observations and its limits. The small, exploratory study leaves both perception and chance findings in play.
items.why: A haunted-room investigation with the apparatus and uncertainty visible. You can compare what people felt with what the instruments recorded, which makes a richer puzzle than a spooky clip alone.

items.title: Pricks
items.summary: An 811-word dark-fantasy story from Nightmare’s November issue, now available to read free. Laura Garrison transforms Sleeping Beauty’s thorns and enchanted sleep into an unsettling modern tale of bodily change and agency. Content includes blood, bodily harm and sexual-threat themes.
items.why: A short piece of fantasy fiction for a spare few minutes. It turns a familiar fairy tale inside out through one strange physical detail, with the ending left for you to discover.

items.title: Do You Want to Be a Saint?
items.summary: Robert Barron’s All Saints sermon asks what sainthood means as the ordinary aim of Christian life. Its companion readings bring together Revelation’s multitude before the Lamb, the hope of becoming like Christ in 1 John, and the Beatitudes.
items.why: An opportunity to read those three passages alongside one another and consider how holiness, grace and the promised vision of God fit together.
items.source: Word on Fire / Bishop Robert Barron

items.title: First Ghosts: From ancient civilisations to Britain
items.summary: A new historical retrospective surveys accounts of the dead from Mesopotamian writing to Roman apparitions and medieval British chronicles. Robert Radakovic includes revenants, phantom armies and Byland Abbey’s tales of spirits asking the living for help. These are traditions and reported encounters.
items.why: For the long view behind modern hauntings. The medieval connection between ghost stories, debts, prayer and the afterlife also gives your theology interest something to meet and question.

items.title: The top 10 scariest RPGs I've ever played⁠—and one I'm too afraid to try
items.summary: Ted Litchfield compares how RPGs create dread, from System Shock 2 and Vampire: The Masquerade – Bloodlines to Lunacid, Labyrinth of the Demon King and Skald. A recent retrospective with major setting and quest spoilers, plus discussion of extreme violence and sexual violence.
items.why: A strong overlap of your retro, RPG and horror interests. The comparisons focus on haunted spaces, lonely exploration and cosmic lore, giving you several different kinds of unsettling world to explore.

items.title: Our Modern Goetheian Deal with the Devil
items.summary: Casey Chalk examines Goethe’s Faust and its treatment of striving, desire and redemption, then challenges its view of human self-improvement from a Christian perspective. Major spoilers for both parts of Faust, including Gretchen’s fate and the ending.
items.why: A literary argument about what actually saves a person, carried through one of the great supernatural bargains. It gives you a concrete story against which to weigh grace, effort and moral transformation.

items.title: Adrian Hicks and the Winchester alien encounter
items.summary: A new retrospective on a councillor’s claimed daylight encounter in 2004. Neil Nixon recounts Hicks’s description of an unusual woman on Winchester High Street and how he connected it with broader beliefs about MJ-12 and government secrecy. Those connections are Hicks’s interpretation.
items.why: An unusually ordinary setting for an extraordinary claim. Following how a brief sighting developed into a much larger conspiracy narrative should scratch the Why Files investigative itch.

items.title: RPGs Coming This Week, November 8–14, 2026 – Nighttime Cartin’
items.summary: Read the Night Cart: The Immortal Plague section for a Gothic journey through 1619 Transylvania, transporting a mysterious plague doctor and deciding when to leave the road for supplies. The preview describes a first-person RPG inspired by King’s Field and Shadow Tower, with Linux among its platforms.
items.why: The haunted countryside, risky detours and early FromSoftware influences fit your atmospheric RPG tastes. Native Linux support is a welcome extra for something you might actually play.
items.source: RPGFan / Mike Salbato, Matt Wardell and Audra Bowling

items.title: Ep 87 | ‘Galahad and the Grail’ — Malcolm Guite
items.summary: Malcolm Guite joins Tod Worner to discuss his Arthurian epic ballad Galahad and the Grail, the opening volume of Merlin’s Isle. The conversation connects the knights’ adventure with Christian virtues and sacramental imagery, offering a route into the book.
items.why: For fantasy reading beyond news and opinions, here is an introduction to a substantial tale in verse. Arthurian wonder and Christian symbolism make a natural meeting point for your interests.
items.source: Word on Fire / Tod Worner and Malcolm Guite

items.category: A Song of Ice and Fire · older gem
items.title: Ragnarök vs The Long Night
items.summary: Older gem from August 2025. History of Westeros compares the Long Night with Norse stories of world-ending winter and fire, then considers volcanic winters, plague and cultural memory. Book spoilers through the published novels. Literary parallels and predictions remain interpretations.
items.why: A deeper Westeros rabbit hole joining mythology, ruined civilisations and environmental catastrophe. The appeal is tracing how remembered disasters might turn into prophecy and lore.
